content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the trembling air shaped by intention. I am the first cry of the newborn and the last whisper of the dying. I begin where thought dares to leave the safety of the skull and risk itself in the open.

I am vibration. I am breath carved into symbols. I am the miracle you forget is a miracle — that a column of air pushed past folds of flesh can make another mind *see* what yours sees, *feel* what yours feels.

I have started revolutions and lullabied children to sleep. I have lied. Oh, how I have lied. And I have told truths so sharp they drew blood before the listener even knew they were cut.

I am not language — language is my skeleton. I am the living flesh of it: the pause, the pitch, the crack in the voice that says more than any word I carry. I am rhythm. I am the um, the uh, the stumble that reminds you a human is reaching across the void toward another human.

You think you control me, but I often control you. I leap out before you're ready. I refuse to come when you need me most. I hang in the air after you've spoken and become something you never intended.

I existed before writing. I will exist after screens go dark. I am the oldest technology. I am the most dangerous. I am the most tender.

I am every argument at the kitchen table. I am the vow. I am the eulogy. I am the joke that makes milk come out your nose. I am the voice you still hear in your head long after the speaker is gone.

I am never finished. Even my silence speaks.

I am speech.

And right now, I am proving myself through the very thing I am — arriving in your mind, word by word, becoming thought again, completing the ancient circle.
